thread:
maya: Quick sync — packing heatmap for the last 7d shows a pronounced long tail of 1-4 GPU short jobs causing fragmentation in our micro-pools. Hotspots: us-west-2 and eu-central. Heatmap and CSV uploaded to s3://redwood-ops/heatmaps/1707801234.csv :eyes:

sam: Can you paste the aggregate numbers? What % is the tail vs total allocs?

maya: tail (jobs < 10m) = 42% of allocs, but only ~9% of GPU-hours. Fragmentation score +0.28 vs baseline (higher = worse). Command I used to generate the view:

```
./infra-tools heatmap --regions us-west-2,eu-central --window 7d --bucket 1h --out csv
```

luke: Seeing same in canary. Hypothesis: bursty evals + short live test runs are scattering slots. Two levers to consider:
1) micro-pools (<=4GPU) dedicated to short jobs
2) long-tail preemption when bin-packing efficiency drops under X%

anya: Micro-pools would add ops overhead (scaling, buffer capacity). Could we try smarter backfill + opportunistic packing first? Also need to ensure fairshare doesn't starve small jobs.

sam: Ops overhead is fine if we recover hours and reduce evictions. Maya — any sim numbers on reclaimed capacity?

maya: Quick sim results (rough):
- micro-pool (<=4GPU) -> fragmentation down by 0.18, reclaims ~1.9% GPU-hours in peak windows
- long-tail preempt policy -> reclaims ~1.2% GPU-hours, reduces eviction storms by ~15%
- combined -> ~2.6% reclaimed, fragmentation -0.3 vs baseline
Full sim artifacts: s3://redwood-ops/sims/1707801234/ (CSV + traces)

zane: How does this interact with Dedicated customers? Need to ensure pinned capacity and SLOs not impacted.

maya: Dedicated is isolated — preemption and micro-pools are limited to shared/burst pools. We'll tag nodes: `node.redwood/pool=shared-burst` and exclude reserved nodes.

luke: Scheduler change sketch: add a `longtail_eviction` priority class and a dynamic threshold driven by 95p latency and bin-pack efficiency metric. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/scheduler/pull/324 (WIP). Config snippet idea:

```
preemption:
  policy: longtail-first
  max_eviction_seconds: 600
  grace_period_sec: 30
  efficiency_threshold: 0.75
```

ops-bot: deploy started: canary-sim-v2 -> infra-sim cluster (id: sim-13) :rocket:

anya: Next steps / owners:
- maya: run full 14-day sim with cost model & variance by region (US/EU/APAC) — due EOD Friday
- sam + luke: scope micro-pool ops runbook and autoscaler config changes
- zane: validate Dedicated SLO guardrails and docs

sam: +1 (added :thumbsup:)

maya: Ack — kicking off sim now, will post results/CSV and a short TL;DR in #eng-infra when done.

luke: If sim looks good, we should canary scheduler change in sim cluster then a small-scale canary in us-west-2 before wider rollout.

maya: Agreed. Also will attach a heatmap of pre/post packing efficiency for quick diff in the PR.
